name: Abis ibn Rabi'a al-Nakha'i

nisbas.en: al-Nakha'i, of the tribe of al-Nakha' (a branch of Madhhij)

orthography.spelled: Abis: with a pointed ba carrying a kasra, then an unpointed sin (عابِس).
homographs: Abis ibn Rabi'a al-Ghutayfi, a Companion who was present at the conquest of Egypt; the Taqrib (entry 3053) says whoever merged the two erred

diedNote: No year of death is recorded in the rijal works; the Shamela record places it between 81 and 90 AH without naming an authority

taqrib.en: Reliable; a mukhadram (lived in both the pre-Islamic period and Islam without meeting the Prophet ﷺ); of the second generation.

role: Mukhadram; eyewitness of Umar at the Black Stone

teachers.name: Umar ibn al-Khattab
teachers.source: Sahih al-Bukhari 1597 and the parallels; Abu Dawud: 'a pre-Islamic man who heard from Umar' (Tahdhib al-Kamal 13/472)

students.name: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abis, his son
students.source: Sahih Muslim (Book of Zuhd), Abd al-Rahman from his father from A'isha; Shamela narrator record 3030

verdicts.ar: هو من مذحج، وكان ثقة، له أحاديث يسيرة
verdicts.en: He is of Madhhij; he was reliable and had a small number of hadith. Ibn Sa'd placed him in the first class of the Kufans.
A man of the pre-Islamic period who heard from Umar.

flags.label: Counted among the Companions by some
flags.detail: Abu Nu'aym al-Isbahani, Ibn Manda and others listed an Abis ibn Rabi'a among the Companions; Ibn Hajar's Taqrib treats that man as a separate person, Abis ibn Rabi'a al-Ghutayfi, who was at the conquest of Egypt, and warns against merging the two. This narrator is the Kufan mukhadram who heard Umar but did not meet the Prophet ﷺ.

bio: A Kufan of al-Nakha' old enough to have lived before Islam, who heard Umar and A'isha but never met the Prophet ﷺ, which is what makes him a mukhadram. He saw Umar kiss the Black Stone and reported the caliph's words, and the parallel versions in Muslim, al-Nasa'i and al-Tirmidhi preserve his own framing: 'I saw Umar'. His younger kinsman Ibrahim al-Nakha'i carried the report on, so two men of al-Nakha' stand side by side in the chain.

provenance.ref: Shamela narrator record 3030, drawing on Tahdhib al-Kamal 13/472, Tahdhib al-Tahdhib 2/250 and Ikmal Tahdhib al-Kamal 7/98
